subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trusted host-read boundary for outbound-staged generated HTML?
rationale: The code review found no concrete bypass in the current patch, but accepting persistent provenance for local HTML host-read is a security lifecycle choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
options.body: Approve the SQLite sha256+size provenance lifecycle as the supported way to preserve generated-HTML trust through outbound staging after the branch is rebased cleanly.

options.title: Require A Narrower Lifecycle
options.body: Ask for a different marker ownership, cleanup, TTL, or failure-mode design before allowing outbound-staged HTML to pass host-read.

options.title: Keep Staged HTML Blocked
options.body: Reject or pause this direction and keep generated HTML delivery fail-closed after staging, preserving the existing temp-root-only trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
recommendation.body: Approve the SQLite sha256+size provenance lifecycle as the supported way to preserve generated-HTML trust through outbound staging after the branch is rebased cleanly.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam and are the clearest history-backed owner for the boundary acceptance call.
